goofy: Refine event client class EventClient class takes an 'event_loop' argument, for some historical reasons, to invoke callbacks in gboject event loop, or from an async IO handler. After dropping support of gtk UI, some clean up can be done on EventClient class. From the viewpoint of the event loop, there are only two event loops: 1. Threaded event loop Process events in a daemon thread. 2. Blocked event loop Process events in the calling thread. In this CL, the EventClient is separated down to two classes, which are ThreadingEventClient and BlockingEventClient. Some utility functions are also added: PostEvent(), PostNewEvent() and SendEvent(). A brief summary for the current usage of event clients: 1. Post an event to the event framework. 2. Send an event, and wait for a specific response. 3. Three places using ThreadingEventClient This will creates a daemon thread to receive events, and call the specified caller properly. 4. test/test_ui.py is the only place using BlockingEventClient This is intended, and important to not lose any events. If using ThreadingEventClient here, the background thread might eat events like goofy:end_test unexpectedly. This is indeed the root cause of chromium:320142. BUG=none TEST=make test TEST=manually run goofy on a DUT Change-Id: I81b9e258f94938a2f9b6043e187cdfe69577d191 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/697167 Commit-Ready: Shen-En Shih <petershih@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shen-En Shih <petershih@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Pi-Hsun Shih <pihsun@chromium.org>

test: Remove event_queue argument from EventClient class The 'event_queue', along with the 'callback' parameter, are kinda confusing at the first glance. The original design is: 1. If the 'callback' is specified, and 'event_queue' is not specified, then call 'callback' when an event arrives. 2. If the 'callback' is specified, and 'event_queue' is a Queue, then put a lambda of call-the-callback-with-arriving-event to the queue. In this case, the 'callback' should not be called upon event arrival. 3. If the 'callback' is not specified, do nothing when an event arrives. It is found that, only one usage of 'event_queue' across the repo. In this CL, the 'event_queue' argument is removed from the EventClient classes, which should make the interface more clear. Also, the caller is still clean and maybe more clear. The only difference is to pass a lambda to the 'callback' argument. BUG=none TEST=make test Change-Id: I9e0b8b9df542b80583ea6ed058da8738e37b221d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/702176 Commit-Ready: Shen-En Shih <petershih@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shen-En Shih <petershih@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Pi-Hsun Shih <pihsun@chromium.org>

shill: reduce number of bucket for *.ExpiredLeaseLengthSeconds metrics shill records *.ExpiredLeaseLengthSeconds metrics for various network types (e.g. Ethernet, WiFi). Each of these metrics is recorded as a count histogram and tracks the DHCP lease length for a network of a particular type when the lease expires without the DHCP client being able to renew it. The maximum of the count histogram for *.ExpiredLeaseLengthSeconds is set to 604800 (the total number of seconds in 7 days) while the number of bucket is set to 604801, which far exceeds the maximum bucket count (16384) specified by the Chrome metrics library. [1] states: "By default count histograms bucket sizes scale exponentially so you can get fine granularity when the numbers are small yet still reasonable resolution for larger numbers. The macros default to 50 buckets (or 100 buckets for histograms with wide ranges) which is appropriate for most purposes." This CL reduces the bucket count for *.ExpiredLeaseLengthSeconds to 100 as recommended by [1]. [1] https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src.git/+/HEAD/tools/metrics/histograms/README.md BUG=chromium:738122 TEST=Run unit tests. Change-Id: I0bf49e5d1e316efebe6de6ea5b078588c192b57b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/557297 Commit-Ready: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: x86/kvm: Move kvm_fastop_exception to .fixup section When compiling the kernel with the '-frecord-gcc-switches' flag, objtool complains: arch/x86/kvm/emulate.o: warning: objtool: .GCC.command.line+0x0: special: can't find new instruction And also the kernel fails to link. The problem is that the 'kvm_fastop_exception' code gets placed into the throwaway '.GCC.command.line' section instead of '.text'. Exception fixup code is conventionally placed in the '.fixup' section, so put it there where it belongs. BUG=chromium:769037 TEST="Build kvm with -frecord-gcc-switches and without -g" Change-Id: Ie88a4f0e637a1be403c3d74779004012d44d78d3 Reported-and-tested-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net> Signed-off-by: Josh Poimboeuf <jpoimboe@redhat.com> Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/9984845/) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/699641
